cards.explanation: The answer is truth or righteousness. These people swear by the LORD's name and invoke the God of Israel, "…but not in truth or righteousness…" (Isaiah 48:1). Saying the right words is the easy part, friends. The LORD is looking at what's behind them, and He says it's missing.
The answer is that suddenly they came to pass. The LORD says, "Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass." (Isaiah 48:3). He had foretold them long ago, friends, and then He acted.

The answer is stubborn. The LORD says, "For I knew that you are stubborn; your neck is iron and your forehead is bronze." (Isaiah 48:4). Then He says, "Therefore I declared it to you long ago…" (Isaiah 48:5). So the early warning came with that knowledge behind it, bakers.

The answer is False. The LORD declared it long ago "…so that you could not claim, ‘My idol has done this; my carved image and molten god has ordained it.’" (Isaiah 48:5). He wasn't handing them an excuse, friends. He was shutting the door on one.

The answer is new and hidden things. The LORD says, "From now on I will tell you of new things, hidden things unknown to you." (Isaiah 48:6). The old things already happened, bakers. Now He's got something fresh to say.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "They are created now, and not long ago; you have not heard of them before today." (Isaiah 48:7). It's the first time hearing it, friends, so nobody gets to say they saw it coming.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "You have never heard; you have never understood; for a long time your ears have not been open." (Isaiah 48:8). Those ears had been shut a good while, bakers. So the card has it backwards.

The answer is for the sake of His name. The LORD says, "For the sake of My name I will delay My wrath…" (Isaiah 48:9). He gives the reason Himself, friends. And look, it comes right after He calls them deceitful and rebellious, and He still holds it back.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "for the sake of My praise I will restrain it, so that you will not be cut off." (Isaiah 48:9). He holds His wrath back, bakers, and He says that's so they won't be cut off.

The answer is in the furnace of affliction. The LORD says, "I have tested you in the furnace of affliction." (Isaiah 48:10). A furnace, friends, and not a gentle one. I think that sounds like a hard place to be.
The answer is False. The LORD says, "for how can I let Myself be defamed? I will not yield My glory to another." (Isaiah 48:11). He won't hand it over to anyone else, bakers.
